newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares finished slightly firmer, but came off their morning highs on profit-taking in late trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
Wall Street's rise by 173 points on Tuesday had propelled the industrials higher in early trade with some dealers welcoming the bouyancy while others predicted a breather towards close of trade.
"We saw really big gains this morning. The market really ran but it has drifted off," one dealer said.
Another dealer added: "There has been a little bit of profit taking at the end".

The dealers said underlying sentiment remained positive but most market players were cautious ahead of economic data -- money supply, private sector credit growth extension and trade figures -- due out on Thursday and Friday.
Dealers said data for the March consumer price index, money market shortage data and the inflation figures released on Wednesday had been better than expected.

"I think sentiment has been buoyed by the CPI figure which is better than expected on the equity side, but for a clear direction as to interest rates in the second half of the year we are looking to the credit extension figures out on Friday and money supply figures," a dealer said.
Volumes were high with 891 million rand worth of shares traded in active trade which saw some selected stocks trade well over a million shares in bookover buys, dealers added.
The industrial index closed 40.3 points up or 0.48 percent at 8,414.8, and the all-share index added 14.3 points to 7,080.2.

Among stocks which traded higher were Dimension Data which added 65 cents to 15.35 rand with 3.4 million shares exhanging hands and Corpgro which was unchanged at 34 rand with 30 million shares traded on the stock.
Jeff Liebesman, Corpgro's chief executive, told Reuters the shares had been bought by an overseas institution.
"I understand that it is an offshore institution that has bought them...it's a very nice stake, but percentage wise it's no a big deal. (We have in issue) around 1.8 billion shares," Liebesman said.
He declined to comment further.
On the bullion board, dealers said golds lacked interest on the back of some weakeness in the yellow metal's price which for most of Wednesday stood at $340 an ounce.
They said some dissapointment from poor gold quarterlies had also permeated through to the market, although some discounting of them had already started. Gold was last bid at $340.80.
"Golds were not looking too good today. I think the golds were down on the gold price and the results. JCI's results were quite shocking and the market doesn't like them whatsoever," one dealer said.
JCI said on Tuesday there had been a 67 percent drop in its profits to 44.24 million rand in the March quarter from 132.89 million in the three months to December, 1996.
It said gold production fell by 8.9 percent to 10,676kg from 11,724kg in the previous quarter.
The gold index ended down 31.6 points or 2.50 percent at 1,231.8.
Kloof was down 75 cents to close at 32.10, Driefontein lost 115 cents to 38.15 rand and Goldfields added 200 cents to 113.00 rand.
Near-dated equity futures also cheered Wall Street's climb early on Wednesday but gold futures were off, held down at weaker levels by a dull bullion price and a steady rand, dealers said.
The June industrial contract was last at 8,255/60 from 8,220, the all-share contract was at 6,560/68 from 6,565 and the gold index was down 15 points at 870/90 from 890 settlement.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
